description: A five-panel composite figure that mixes EBSD maps with pole figures, taken from the tensile-fractured 15Mn5Ni low-density steel. (a) is a grayscale EBSD image-quality (IQ) map of the longitudinal cross-section with a 25 µm scale bar: dark, elongated B2 stringers lie in a lighter γ matrix, two yellow arrows mark stringers that appear cracked across their narrow dimension, and a black rectangle delimits the region analysed further. (b) is the magnified OIM/IPF orientation map of that box (10 µm scale bar, IPF colour triangle at top right) with two black squares labelled I and II. (c) is the phase map of the same field (10 µm bar), legend red = γ and blue = B2, showing continuous blue B2 stringers in a red γ matrix. (d) is the KAM map (10 µm bar) whose colour bar reads Min 0 / Max 5, with local misorientation concentrated in green–yellow bands along stringer/matrix interfaces. (e) gives {111} and {110} pole figures for Region-I (cracked B2) and Region-II (non-cracked B2), overlaid with austenite and B2 pole sets. Region-I shows tightly clustered red austenite poles with scattered blue B2 poles, i.e. no shared orientation relationship, while Region-II poles are sparse — the figure argues that loss of a γ/B2 orientation relationship at a B2 stringer coincides with cracking there, restricting slip transfer and harming ductility.
measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation (KAM), colour-bar range 0 to 5 (unit not printed)
IPF orientation (Euler colour key) of γ and B2 grains
phase fraction/area of γ versus B2 (qualitative from phase map)
pole figure pole density of {111} and {110} for austenite and B2
scale bars: 25 µm (a), 10 µm (b, c, d)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a grayscale EBSD image-quality (IQ) map of the longitudinal cross-section of the tensile-fractured sample, with a 25 µm scale bar and elongated dark stringers within a lighter matrix.
Two yellow arrows are drawn on panel (a) pointing to stringer locations, and a black rectangle in the lower-left marks the region presented in panels (b)-(d).
Panel (b) carries a 10 µm scale bar and an IPF colour-triangle legend, with two black boxes labelled I and II.
Panel (c) is a two-colour phase map with the printed legend red = γ and blue = B2, showing blue B2 stringers elongated within a red γ matrix.
Panel (d) is a KAM map whose colour bar is labelled 'Min 0' and 'Max 5'; the numeric unit (degrees) is not printed on the figure.
In panel (d) the highest local misorientation values (green-to-yellow) are concentrated in elongated bands following the B2 stringer/γ matrix interfaces, while grain interiors remain low (blue).
Panel (e) contains {111} and {110} pole figures for Region-I (top row) and Region-II (bottom row); Region-I poles are clustered/multiple whereas Region-II pole figures show only a few isolated poles.
The caption states that (a) is an EBSD-IQ map of the cross-section microstructure of tensile fractured 15Mn5Ni alloy and that (b) is a magnified OIM map showing cracked B2.
The caption states that (c) is a phase map and (d) is a KAM map showing slip transfer and strain distribution in γ and B2.
The caption states that (e) shows the orientation relationship (OR) between γ and B2 in Region I and Region II of Fig. 10b, which contain cracked and non-cracked B2 respectively.
The citing text asserts that some B2 stringers have cracked in a direction perpendicular to the tensile axis at specific locations (arrows in Fig. 10a).
The citing text asserts that cracks formed in B2 stringers that exhibit no orientation relationship with the austenite grain, attributed to restricted slip transfer at the γ/B2 interface.
The citing text asserts that substantial strain accumulation and cracking occurred in some deformed B2 grains of specific orientations.

subfigures.description: Grayscale EBSD image-quality (IQ) map of the longitudinal cross-section of the tensile-fractured 15Mn5Ni specimen, 25 µm scale bar. Dark elongated stringers run roughly parallel through a lighter matrix; two yellow arrows point to locations on these stringers and a black rectangle in the lower-left marks the region magnified in (b)-(d).

Magnified OIM/IPF colour orientation map of the boxed region in (a), 10 µm scale bar, with an IPF colour triangle key at top right. Two small black rectangles are labelled I and II; cracks and colour-graded grains are visible within the mapped field.
EBSD phase map of the same field, 10 µm scale bar, with legend red = γ (austenite) and blue = B2. Two continuous, elongated blue B2 stringers are embedded in the red γ matrix.

KAM (kernel average misorientation) map of the same field, 10 µm scale bar, colour bar labelled Min 0 to Max 5 (unit not printed). Local misorientation is highest (green–yellow) in bands along the stringer/matrix interfaces and grain boundaries, and lowest (blue) inside grain interiors.

Two rows of stereographic pole figures: Region-I (top) and Region-II (bottom), each with a {111} and a {110} projection, overlaid with two pole symbol sets and a legend reading 'Austenite' and 'B2'. Region-I {111} shows four tightly clustered pole groups plus scattered poles; Region-II pole figures contain only a few sparse poles. Which symbol colour corresponds to which phase is not clearly resolved at this resolution.
